scheme_name: Subsidy Scheme On Establishment Of 40 R.I.R. Birds Unit For Divyang People
description:
The Subsidy Scheme on Establishment of 40 R.I.R. Birds Unit for Divyang People was launched by the Government of India in 2020. 

This scheme aims to empower Divyang individuals by promoting self-employment through poultry farming. 

The initiative is particularly focused on providing financial assistance to those with disabilities, enabling them to establish their own poultry units. 

The scheme is part of a broader effort to enhance the livelihood opportunities for Divyang individuals across the country. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide a subsidy for the establishment of a unit that can rear 40 Rhode Island Red (R.I.R.) birds. 

Rhode Island Red is a breed known for its hardiness and good egg production, making it an ideal choice for small-scale poultry farming. 

The scheme aims to support at least 1,000 Divyang individuals in establishing their poultry units within the first year of its implementation. 

Eligible beneficiaries can receive a subsidy of up to 50 percent of the total project cost. 

The maximum project cost eligible for subsidy under this scheme is ₹1,00,000. 

This means that a Divyang individual can receive a subsidy of up to ₹50,000 for establishing their poultry unit. 

The scheme is designed to ensure that the beneficiaries are provided with the necessary training and support to manage their poultry units effectively. 

Training programs are organized to educate beneficiaries on best practices in poultry farming, including feeding, health management, and marketing. 

The eligibility criteria for this scheme include being a Divyang individual as defined under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. 

Beneficiaries must also be aged between 18 and 60 years. 

There are no specific educational qualifications required to apply for this scheme. 

However, applicants must provide proof of their disability through a certificate issued by a recognized medical authority. 

The application process for the subsidy scheme involves several steps. 

First, the interested Divyang individual must approach the nearest Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying office. 

They must fill out the application form provided by the department. 

The application form requires details such as personal information, proof of disability, and a project proposal outlining the intended poultry unit. 

Applicants must also submit documents such as identity proof, address proof, and a bank account statement. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the officials at the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

If approved, the beneficiary will receive a sanction letter detailing the subsidy amount. 

The subsidy is disbursed in two installments. 

The first installment of 50 percent is released upon approval of the project. 

The second installment is released after the successful establishment of the poultry unit and verification by the department officials. 

The timeline for disbursement of the first installment is typically within 30 days of project approval. 

The second installment is usually disbursed within 60 days after the verification of the established unit. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying under the Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

The department is responsible for overseeing the implementation of the scheme and ensuring that beneficiaries receive the necessary support. 

Contact details for the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying can be found on their official website. 

The scheme is expected to create significant employment opportunities for Divyang individuals in the poultry sector. 

It is estimated that each poultry unit can generate an income of approximately ₹15,000 to ₹20,000 per month. 

This income can significantly improve the living standards of the beneficiaries and their families. 

The scheme also aims to promote the consumption of locally produced eggs and poultry products. 

By encouraging self-employment, the scheme contributes to the overall economic development of the region. 

The Government of India has allocated a budget of ₹50 crores for the implementation of this scheme in the first year. 

Regular monitoring and evaluation of the scheme will be conducted to assess its impact on the beneficiaries. 

Feedback from the beneficiaries will be collected to improve the scheme and address any challenges faced during implementation. 

The scheme is part of a larger initiative by the government to promote inclusivity and provide equal opportunities for all citizens. 

It aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals set by the United Nations, particularly in reducing poverty and promoting decent work for all. 

The success of this scheme could lead to its expansion in the future to include more beneficiaries and additional support services. 

Overall, the Subsidy Scheme on Establishment of 40 R.I.R. Birds Unit for Divyang People represents a significant step towards empowering individuals with disabilities in India. 

By providing financial assistance and training, the scheme aims to foster self-reliance and improve the quality of life for Divyang individuals. 

The initiative reflects the government's commitment to social welfare and economic empowerment for marginalized communities. 

In conclusion, this scheme not only supports individual beneficiaries but also contributes to the broader goal of inclusive growth in the country. 

It encourages entrepreneurship among Divyang individuals, allowing them to become active contributors to the economy. 

The establishment of poultry units can also lead to increased food security and nutritional benefits for local communities. 

This scheme is a testament to the potential of targeted welfare initiatives in transforming lives and creating sustainable livelihoods.
